note: Round 2 drops Sharpe from the score and gives annual return 15%, max drawdown 15% and failure rate 70%, so the round-1 choice of anchor_penalty (0.25, picked on a Sharpe era drawdown criterion) was re-derived rather than inherited. Candidates 0, 0.25, 1, 4, 16 were run under the round-2 contract -- WalkForward(252, 20) with weight_drift on -- on sp500(20), ftse100(64) and factors(5), then scored under a simulated field of skfolio optimizers. Two findings decided this: (1) the 70% failure term dominates everything, so the method must simply not fail, and every candidate here survives all folds; (2) across the annual-return and drawdown terms the candidates are nearly tied, which is the familiar signature of sliding along the efficient frontier rather than improving it. Under that tie the choice was made on compliance distance, and 4.0 sits furthest from the three prohibited books among the settings that do not give up rank. anchor_penalty = 0 is explicitly excluded: on a 5-asset panel denoising is skipped and shrinkage is weak, the result correlates 0.999 with the prohibited SCM minimum variance portfolio, and that is a violation rather than a near miss. Evidence: research/round2/.
short_selling_note: The brief permits shortselling, so the permission is a parameter (allow_short, short_cap) and not an assumption; the shipped setting leaves it off. That is a measurement, not a default: the full sweep over (anchor_penalty, short_cap) is in reports/round2_short_sweep.{json,txt}. Three facts decide it. (1) Full investment pins net exposure at 1, so gross exposure is exactly 1 + 2 * (total short): a short budget and a gross cap of 1 cannot both bind, and any short position pushes gross above the leverage limit. (2) At the shipped anchor_penalty = 4.0 the short budget barely binds anyway -- on sp500(20) a cap of 0.05 moves annual return from 16.407% to 16.365% and max drawdown from 57.001% to 56.535%, i.e. both economically negligible, while gross rises from 1.000 to 1.156. In the rank-percentile simulation those settings score 0.509-0.516, and the gap between a clean run and a broken one is about 0.51 of total score (every zero-failure candidate shares r_fail = 0.523, while HRP/HERC at 99.8% failures score 0.012). The simulation contains no candidate with a failure rate between 1% and 99%, so it prices the clean-versus-broken gap but NOT the marginal cost of a first failed fold; treat it as an order-of-magnitude statement, not a per-fold price. The option buys nothing and risks the dominant term. (3) The large drawdown reductions (sp500: 57% to 31%) are only reachable at anchor_penalty = 0, which is the setting already excluded for reproducing the prohibited SCM minimum variance portfolio; shorting a pure variance-and-anchor objective can only push the book toward the minimum-variance vertex. The option is therefore implemented, verified to machine precision and swept, but not enabled.
